content: 1. Tobramycin and OnabotulinumtoxinA: Tobramycin enhances the effects of onabotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction may lead to excessive neuromuscular weakness and increased systemic anticholinergic effects. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 2. Tobramycin and Aminoglycosides: Co-administration of tobramycin with other aminoglycosides may potentiate the effects of botulinum toxins, increasing the risk of profound neuromuscular weakness and systemic anticholinergic side effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Tobramycin and Oxaliplatin: Both tobramycin and oxaliplatin can increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are recommended when these agents are used together. 4. Tobramycin and Peramivir: Tobramycin increases the levels of peramivir by reducing renal clearance. Additionally, caution is advised when peramivir is co-administered with nephrotoxic drugs. 5. Tobramycin and Phenobarbital: Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of tobramycin by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 6. Tobramycin and Phenytoin: Phenytoin reduces the levels or effects of tobramycin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Tobramycin and Polymyxin B: Co-administration of tobramycin with polymyxin B increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are required. 8. Tobramycin and PrabotulinumtoxinA: Tobramycin enhances the effects of prabotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Tobramycin and Quercetin: Quercetin decreases the levels or effects of tobramycin by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Tobramycin and Rifampin: Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of tobramycin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Tobramycin and RimabotulinumtoxinB: Tobramycin enhances the effects of rimabotulinumtoxinB through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of excessive neuromuscular weakness and systemic anticholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 12. Tobramycin and Ritonavir: Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tobramycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Tobramycin and Sirolimus: Sirolimus increases the levels or effects of tobramycin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Tobramycin and Sodium Picosulfate/Magnesium Oxide/Anhydrous Citric Acid: Tobramycin reduces the effects of this combination by altering metabolism. Antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by disrupting colonic bacterial flora required for drug activation. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Tobramycin and Magnesium Sulfate/Potassium Chloride: Co-administration with medications causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Tobramycin and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of tobramycin by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Tobramycin and Streptozocin: Both tobramycin and streptozocin increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are required. 18. Tobramycin and Tacrolimus: Tacrolimus increases the levels or effects of tobramycin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Additionally, both agents increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 19. Tobramycin and Teicoplanin: Co-administration of tobramycin with teicoplanin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 20. Tobramycin and Tenofovir DF: Both tobramycin and tenofovir DF increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Tobramycin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely.
